predecessors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the whole Eastern Roman Empire of 632: Anatolia, Thrace, the Levant, Egypt, Africa and the Italian exarchate, as the last Eastern Roman shape holds them

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: the Despotate of the Morea, the last Palaiologan land, taken in May 1460

ledger.x: 633: the Eastern Roman state continues as the Byzantine Empire, a hand-over and not a founding.
633: the Ghassanid client relation ends with Cliopatria's last Ghassanid row (510-633).
634: the Arab conquest of Syria begins.
Late 637: Antioch and northern Syria fall.
September 642: the treaty of Alexandria ends the first Egyptian campaign (the fleet's recovery of Alexandria in 645-646 is a separate pair of events).
647: the Arabs invade the Exarchate of Africa.
648: the Arabs leave Africa for a tribute.
657: during the First Fitna the Armenian princes return to Byzantine overlordship.
662: Constans II moves the capital to Syracuse.
668: the seat is back at Constantinople.
681: the Bulgars are recognised in Moesia.
695: the Umayyad campaign against Carthage begins.
698: Carthage falls and with it Byzantine Africa.
698: the fighting for Africa ends with the fall of Carthage.
718: the western Mediterranean outposts disappear from Cliopatria's shape.
732: Corsica drops out of Cliopatria's shape.

c. 738: Liutprand takes Ravenna for a time. 'in c. 738, the city was taken for a time by the Lombard king Liutprand.' The counterpart is the Lombard kingdom, Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Italy' row (587-774).
788: Cliopatria adds 89 cells in inland Macedonia.
827: Crete falls to the Andalusian exiles.
840: Sardinia drops out of Cliopatria's shape.
840: the Muslims seize Taranto, their first base on the Italian mainland.
855-856: the Byzantines reconquer the Thracian cities.
860: Cliopatria's shape restores 12 cells at Kavala.
29 August 870: the Muslim fleet takes Malta, the last of the islands around Sicily in Byzantine hands.
902: Taormina falls, the end of Byzantine Sicily.
922: Bizye. 'in 922 they were victorious at Pigae, burning much of the Golden Horn and seizing Bizye.'
944: Edessa. 'these culminated in the reconquest of Edessa (944).' Confidence 2: the page does not say who held it or whether the city was annexed; Cliopatria draws Edessa as Byzantine only from 970.
962: Nikephoros II in Cilicia and northern Syria.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)
Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)
Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 971: Boris II brought to Constantinople; the campaign ends with the annexation.
1000: Basil II takes the old Bulgarian capitals.
1002: Vidin. Basil 'occupied the length of the military road from the western Haemus Mountains to the Danube' and 'laid siege to Vidin, which fell after a prolonged resistance'.

ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 1015: Cliopatria adds 218 cells at Lovech, in the middle of the Kleidion campaign (1014-1018).
1018: the Bulgarian war ends with the submission of the last Bulgarian forces.

December 1025: Basil II dies (15 December) and the Croatian tributary relation lapses with him ('Croatia remained a tributary state to Basil until his death in 1025'); the empire 'stretched from southern Italy to the Caucasus and from the Danube to the Levant'.
1028: Tartus drops out of Cliopatria's shape.

1045: Ani. Gagik II 'surrendered Ani to the Byzantines in 1045'; 'Ani was then annexed to the theme of Iberia which was renamed 'Iberia and Ani''. In 1041-1042 he had been 'obliged to cede his domain to the empire in exchange for a domain in Cappadocia'; 'In 1044, the Byzantines twice invaded Ani but failed to conquer…
1046: Cliopatria drops 43 cells in northern Apulia.
1056: Cliopatria drops 30 cells around Podgorica, the Dukljan lands.
c. 1064: Kars. Gagik-Abas 'was constrained to cede his lands to the Byzantines and retreat to Anatolia'.
1065: Kars. 'only to see Kars captured by the Turks in 1065.'
1066: Cliopatria drops Calabria and the Stari Ras block.
1066: Raška. Page silent; the counterpart is the nearest dossier-state (Dukljan sphere); confidence 1.

c. 1085: the Normans are out. 'Forced to retreat to Italy, Bohemond lost all the territory gained by the Normans in the campaign.' The sentence is undated; 1085 is the year Cliopatria's shape shows nothing of the occupation. Confidence 1.
John II's Cilicia: 'John successfully captured the southern coast of Anatolia as far as Antioch.'
1167: the lands of the Hungarian war.
1168: the end of Cliopatria's Grand Principality row.
1187: the treaty ends the first phase of the revolt.
1188: Cliopatria drops Sirmium, Bosnia and Dalmatia.
1204: Thrace outside the city passes to the Latin Empire.
1204: Sinope, Samsun and Limnia on the Pontic coast go to Alexios Komnenos.
1204: David Komnenos takes the Paphlagonian coast.
1204: Macedonia and Thessaly north of Domokos pass to Boniface of Montferrat's Kingdom of Thessalonica.
April 1204: the Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople.
April 1204: Alexios and David Komnenos take Trebizond and its province.

c. 1205: Michael Komnenos Doukas sets up in Epirus and the old province of Nicopolis leaves the empire. 'From his base at Arta, Michael proceeded to expand his control over most of the region of Epirus.' The page has Michael leave Boniface of Montferrat for Epirus in 1204 and starts his rule as ruler of Epirus c.…
1205: Attica and Boeotia pass to Otto de la Roche's Duchy of Athens.
25 July 1261: Constantinople is recaptured and the Nicaean state, with the city, becomes the restored empire.
Early 1262: Monemvasia, Mystras and the Mani are handed to the Byzantines.
By 1264 the rest of Laconia is Byzantine except Lacedaemon.

c. 1280: Nikephoros I of Epirus loses his holdings in Albania to the Byzantines. 'With Charles' defeat soon after, Nikephoros lost his holdings in Albania to the Byzantines.' The page dates only the 1279 vassalage to Charles of Anjou ('In 1279 Nikephoros acknowledged himself Charles' vassal and surrendered Butrinto')…
1305: Cliopatria drops 271 cells at Kütahya and Thracian cells at Burgas.
1318: Ioannina and the north of Epirus declare for the Byzantine emperor.
1320: Karytaina and the eastern half of the barony of Karytaina fall to the Byzantines under Andronikos Asen.

c. 1325: John II Orsini recovers the north as a Byzantine despot. He 'was allowed to establish his control over all of Epirus in exchange for recognizing Byzantine suzerainty' and 'was awarded the title of despotes by the Byzantine emperor'; the page gives no year for either and dates his rule 1323-1335. Confidence 1…
1326: Bursa. 'the Ottomans succeeded in taking Bursa from the Byzantines in 1326.'
1329: Chios. 'In 1329, the Byzantines recaptured Chios'; the page names no previous holder.
1337: the Bithynian front ends with the fall of Nicomedia.
1339: the Arta rebellion for Nikephoros II takes the Epirote heartland out of Byzantine hands.
1340: Andronikos III suppresses the revolt and Epirus is Byzantine again.
1352: the first Ottoman foothold in Europe.
Spring 1418: Theodore II Palaiologos takes Messenia and Elis from Centurione II Zaccaria.
14 September 1423: the Despot Andronikos Palaiologos hands Thessalonica to Venice.
1 May 1428: Glarentza, the Tocco port in Elis, passes to Constantine Palaiologos.
1429: Thomas Palaiologos besieges Centurione II Zaccaria in Chalandritsa and the prince gives it up.
1430: 'the Despotate of the Morea expanded to incorporate the entire peninsula in 1430.'
July 1430: the Archbishop's castle of Patras surrenders and the city is Byzantine again.
1432: Centurione II Zaccaria dies and his last barony passes to Thomas Palaiologos, ending the Principality of Achaea.
May 1453: with Constantinople lost the only Byzantine land is the Morea, held by the emperor's brothers Demetrios and Thomas Palaiologos; the seat moves to Mystras (identity.capitals).
1460: the last Byzantine land passes to the Ottomans.

wars.name: Arab conquest of Syria and Palestine
wars.outcome: Arab victory: Damascus in 634, Jerusalem in April 637, Gaza in summer 637, Antioch and northern Syria in late 637, Mesopotamia and Armenia overrun 638-639, Caesarea Maritima and Ascalon taken 638-639; in December 639 the Muslims 'departed from Palestine to…

wars.name: Arab conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Arab victory: Alexandria 'agreed to give up the city by September 642'; the Byzantine fleet retook it in 645 and lost it again in 646 after the Battle of Nikiou.

wars.name: Arab invasion of the Exarchate of Africa (647-648)
wars.outcome: Arab raid: Tripolitania conquered, then Sufetula; the Arabs 'promised ... an annual tribute' and withdrew; the exarchate stayed Byzantine until 698.

wars.name: Arab capture of Cyprus
wars.outcome: Cyprus 'captured in 653' on the Arab-Byzantine page; the Heraclian page has the Arab fleet raiding 'the Byzantine island of Cyprus' in 657.

wars.name: First Arab siege of Constantinople and the Cyzicus campaign
wars.outcome: Byzantine victory at the cost of the Cyzicus peninsula for six years: 'in 672, Muawiya the Caliph captured the peninsula of Cyzicus'; Constantine IV 'began the siege of Constantinople in 674'; in 678 the Saracens withdrew and Muawiya accepted peace.

wars.name: Byzantine-Bulgar war of 680-681
wars.outcome: Bulgar victory: 'In 681 Constantine was forced to acknowledge the Bulgarian state in Moesia'.

wars.name: Justinian II's Slavic campaign
wars.outcome: Byzantine success: 'he sent an expedition against the Slavs between 688 and 689' and 'His success in the west was crowned with a triumphant entry into Thessalonika'

wars.name: Umayyad conquest of Carthage
wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: Carthage 'conquered and destroyed ... between 695 and 698'; (main page) 'In 698, Africa was lost to the Umayyad Caliphate'.

wars.name: Arab siege of Constantinople (717-718)
wars.outcome: The Isaurian page covers the siege of Constantinople and dates its end to 15 August 718; no border moved, so no zone is drawn.

wars.name: Lombard conquest of the Exarchate of Ravenna
wars.outcome: Ravenna taken (Isaurian page) 'in c.

wars.name: Krum's war (Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 809-815)
wars.outcome: Bulgarian gains: Serdica in 809, Develtos and Mesembria in 812, Arkadioupolis and Adrianople in 813; Nikephoros I fell in 811; the thirty-year peace of 815 'specified the border in Thrace'.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Crete
wars.outcome: Andalusian exiles ('Abbasid vassals') conquered Crete in 827; it stayed lost until 961.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Sicily
wars.outcome: Arab victory in stages: Palermo 831, Messina 842, Enna 859, Syracuse 878, Catania 900, Taormina 902, 'the final Greek stronghold'; Sicily had been Byzantine 'for over three hundred years' (both from the Macedonian-dynasty page).

wars.name: Bulgarian-Byzantine wars of the 830s-860s
wars.outcome: Philippopolis (836) and Philippi (837) to the Bulgars; the Thracian cities reconquered in 855-856; Zagora returned to Bulgaria in 863.

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of Apulia and Calabria
wars.outcome: Byzantine gains: Bari 'became Byzantine territory in 876'; Taranto and much of Calabria taken in 880.

wars.name: Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 913-927
wars.outcome: Bulgarian gains in Thrace (Adrianople 914, Bizye 922), all restored by the peace of 927 ('frontiers restored to those defined in treaties of 897 and 904').

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of Melitene and Edessa
wars.outcome: Byzantine gains: the Emirate of Melitene and the Armenian marches in the 930s; 'the reconquest of Edessa (944)' (Macedonian-dynasty page).

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of Crete
wars.outcome: Byzantine victory: 'Crete was reconquered in 961', 134 years after the Andalusian conquest.

wars.name: Byzantine campaigns in Cilicia and northern Syria
wars.outcome: Byzantine gains: Cilicia and northern Syria 'including the sack of Aleppo' (962); Antioch and the Orontes plain (page undated); the emirate of Aleppo became a vassal during John I's reign (969-976).

wars.name: Byzantine campaign in Bulgaria under John I
wars.outcome: Byzantine victory: Preslav besieged, Boris II brought to Constantinople in 971, and 'The Bulgarian lands in Thrace and lower Moesia now became part of the Byzantine Empire'.

wars.name: Basil II's Bulgarian war
wars.outcome: Byzantine victory: the old Bulgarian capitals in 1000, Vodena, Verrhoia and Servia in 1001, Vidin in 1002, Dyrrhachium in 1005, and Bulgaria 'completely conquered' in 1018; In 986 Samuel 'drove Basil II's army from the field at the Gates of Trajan'.

wars.name: Byzantine-Georgian war over Tao
wars.outcome: Georgia 'occupied Tao in 1015-1016'; the early-1022 treaty 'handed over Tao, Phasiane, Kola, Artaan and Javakheti' to the Empire.

wars.name: Revolt of Peter Delyan
wars.outcome: Byzantine victory: the revolt took 'Nis and Skopje' and Macedonia and Dyrrhachium for a time while Thessalonica held; crushed by 1041.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Byzantine southern Italy
wars.outcome: Norman victory: Apulia, the Salento and Calabria lost (page silent on the years; Cliopatria's shapes 1046, 1056, 1066) and 'In 1071 Bari, the last remaining Byzantine settlement in Italy, was captured by the Normans'.

wars.name: Seljuk capture of Ani and Kars
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory: Ani fell in 1064 ('even after 1064 when Ani fell to the Seljuk Turks') and Kars was captured by the Turks in 1065.

wars.name: Byzantine-Seljuk wars: Manzikert and the loss of Anatolia
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory: Manzikert on 26 August 1071 opened Asia Minor to the Seljuks and Turkomans; Nicaea 1078, Antioch to Philaretos 1078-1084, Smyrna by 1084, the last Anatolian towns by 1091.

wars.name: Norman invasion of the Balkans (1081-1085)
wars.outcome: Norman gains for a time: Dyrrhachium in February 1082, 'most of Macedonia and Thessaly'; 'Bohemond lost all the territory gained by the Normans in the campaign' (page undated; ledger 1085, confidence 1).

wars.name: Komnenian recovery of western Anatolia
wars.outcome: Byzantine gains: the Marmara shore in 1094, Nicaea on 19 June 1097 (surrendered to the Byzantines during the First Crusade) and, under John Doukas, Smyrna, Ephesus, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea and Choma.

wars.name: Byzantine-Hungarian war of 1163-1167
wars.outcome: Byzantine victory at Sirmium (1167): 'With this victory the Kingdom of Hungary was made a vassal of the Empire'; the lands gained are not stated on the page.

wars.name: Uprising of Asen and Peter
wars.outcome: Bulgarian victory: the revolt of 1185 re-founded a Bulgarian state; a treaty of 1186-1187 'effectively recognizing the Second Bulgarian Empire'.

wars.name: Second Bulgarian Empire's conquests
wars.outcome: Bulgarian gains: Sredec (Sofia) and Nis in 1191, Konstanteia and Varna in 1201, most of Slavic Macedonia in 1202.

wars.name: Fourth Crusade
wars.outcome: Crusader victory: the sack of Constantinople in April 1204; 'The crusaders crowned Baldwin I as the ruler of a new Latin Empire'; Venice 'acquired many ports and islands'; the Principality of Achaea 'emerged in southern Greece'; the Greek rump states followed.

wars.name: Reconquest of Constantinople
wars.outcome: Nicaean victory: 'Constantinople was recaptured in 1261 from the Latin Empire by Nicaean forces led by the general Alexios Strategopoulos' (25 July); Michael VIII entered the city on 15 August.

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of the Morea
wars.outcome: Byzantine gains by stages: the eastern Morea ceded after Pelagonia (page undated; ledger 1262), Arcadia (Cliopatria's shape year 1326), 'the last remnants of the Principality of Achaea' in 1428, 'the entire peninsula in 1430'.

wars.name: Serbian conquest of Macedonia
wars.outcome: Serbian victory: 'leaving much of Macedonia in ruin and in the hands of the newly created Serbian Empire' (undated, 1340s).

wars.name: Byzantine-Ottoman wars: Bithynia
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: the siege of Nicaea began in 1301; Bursa fell in 1326, Nicaea ('In 1331, Nicaea surrendered') and Nicomedia in 1337.

wars.name: Byzantine-Ottoman wars: Thrace and Macedonia
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory by stages: Tzympe 1352, Kallipolis 1354 (retaken 'temporarily' in 1366), Didymoteichon 1361, Adrianople 1369, Thessalonica 1387, Philadelphia 1390, and 'by 1400, Byzantine Thrace was also lost'.

wars.name: Fall of Constantinople
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: 'An all-out assault captured the city on May 29, 1453'; the page ends the empire there.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Morea
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: 'Mehmed came into the Morea in May 1460' (infobox 'Ottoman conquest: 29 May 1460'); the brothers Demetrios and Thomas Palaiologos had held the Despotate after 1453.

certainty.note: The frontier with the Caliphate was a raided march (Taurus, Cappadocia) and the Balkan interior was Slav-held; the pages opened give no treaty lines.

The Thracian frontier with Bulgaria is sharp after the 815 treaty ('the treaty specified the border in Thrace') and again after the 927 peace ('frontiers restored to those defined in treaties of 897 and 904'); every other frontier stays…
The Danube is a river line from 1018 ('regained its ancient Danubian frontier'); the Anatolian and Balkan frontiers are marches and approximate.
The state holds no land (split into the Nicaean and Latin states); the Nicaean dossier carries the Greek lands.
The Ottoman frontier in Bithynia and Thrace is a moving march; the Morea's frontier with Achaea runs to 1430.
